subject: EU data residency wording + DPA checklist for procurement
messages:
From: Sophie Jensen <sophie.jensen@acme-eu.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: J. Alvarez <jalvarez@acme-eu.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme-eu.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: DPA + residency language for procurement review

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ACME's platform team liked the latency/throughput numbers. Procurement is moving fast and asked for a one-page checklist we can include with the contract packet to make legal/procurement review quicker. Two asks from them:

1) A short plain-language statement about where hosted API customer data may be processed and whether we have an EU-only residency option (they want wording they can paste into their procurement summary).
2) A current subprocessor inventory (they need hosting/ops vendors and whether any are outside the EEA).

Can you send a one-page checklist + the subprocessor list? If you have a draft DPA we can review, please attach.

Ideal timeline: procurement wants something short by Fri EOD CET.

Sophie
Sophie Jensen
Senior Procurement Manager, ACME Technologies

--
Attachment: requirements_from_acme_20260922.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Jensen <sophie.jensen@acme-eu.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: DPA + residency language for procurement review

Sophie — thanks, we can do that. Sending an initial bundle for your procurement pack: plain-language bullets you can paste, the latest subprocessor inventory, and our current DPA draft (attached).

Plain-language statement (short):
- Redwood Inference processes API requests on behalf of customers in our hosted service. By default, request handling may transit through infrastructure in multiple regions for performance and reliability.
- For customers requiring EU-only processing, we offer a hosted residency option that pins inference and associated request metadata to EEA-based compute and storage. This option is configurable at onboarding and subject to a residency addendum in the DPA.
- Subprocessors (hosting, monitoring, observability) are disclosed in our subprocessor inventory; customers can request confirmations or additional safeguards via the DPA.

Procurement checklist (one-page highlights):
- DPA version: attached (DPA_Draft_v3.pdf) — contains residency addendum language.
- Residency option: available (EEA-only) — requires residency addendum + region-specific configuration.
- Data types covered: request payloads, generated outputs, logs/telemetry tied to customer tokens.
- Retention defaults: request logs retained 30 days; configurable via contract for enterprise plans.
- Subprocessors: see attached CSV; flag for non-EEA subprocessors included.
- Security certifications: SOC 2 Type II (summary attached in separate thread)
- Next steps: sign DPA + residency addendum -> confirm residency region -> ops will schedule migration window.

Attachments: DPA_Draft_v3.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_20260920.csv, eu-residency-ui-copy.docx

Let me know if Laura/legal want tighter phrasing for the residency line the ACME procurement team can paste into their internal packet. I can shorten further to 2–3 sentences if needed.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0199

--
Attachment stubs: DPA_Draft_v3.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_20260920.csv; eu-residency-ui-copy.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Jensen <sophie.jensen@acme-eu.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: DPA + residency language for procurement review

Hi Sophie — copying a slightly tightened set of statements your team can paste straight into procurement notes. I also flagged the particular DPA clause numbers so legal can reference them.

Paste-ready summary (one short paragraph):
Redwood Inference operates a hosted API that processes customer requests in cloud infrastructure. We offer an EU-only residency configuration that ensures inference compute and related customer metadata are pinned to EEA-based resources; this option is activated via a residency addendum to the DPA. All subprocessors are listed in our inventory (attached) and any non-EEA subprocessors are disclosed — contractual safeguards and additional technical controls are available on request.

Legal references (for ACME Legal):
- Residency addendum: DPA, Section 3.2
- Subprocessors: DPA, Section 5 and Appendix A (inventory)
- Data retention defaults: DPA, Section 6.1

Sophie — if ACME needs the paragraph shortened further for a single-line procurement summary, suggest: "Redwood offers an EU-only residency configuration (DPA addendum) and discloses subprocessors in the attached inventory."

Also attaching a redline with two small edits to the DPA draft: 1) clarify that telemetry aggregated for service health is pseudonymized by default; 2) add an ops contact for residency migrations.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: DPA_Draft_v3_redline.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Jensen <sophie.jensen@acme-eu.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: DPA + residency language for procurement review

Sophie — quick note from sales: procurement asked whether residency activation affects pricing or lead time. Short answers:
- Pricing: residency is included in our enterprise offering; standard onboarding covers the configuration. There may be additional fees for dedicated capacity or on-prem variants — we won’t surprise you, any extra costs will be in the SOW.
- Lead time: typical residency activation (EEA pinning) is 1–2 weeks after the signed DPA and residency addendum; dedicated migrations take longer and are scoped separately.

Next steps: Sophie, if ACME confirms they want the residency option, we’ll: (1) route DPA to DocuSign, (2) schedule a 30-minute ops kickoff to pick migration window, (3) confirm any SOW items.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

--
